incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a four-year-old legacy smart contract in the Transit Finance cross-chain aggregator.
incidents.impact: $1.9 million in crypto assets stolen. The platform pledged to compensate affected users.

incidents.vector: Hackers exploited a smart contract that interacts with the TON blockchain, the same type of contract abused in a parallel Transit Finance theft on the same day.
incidents.impact: $2.8 million in crypto assets stolen from the platform.

incidents.victim: German university hospitals (Cologne, Freiburg, Heidelberg, Tübingen, Ulm, Mannheim)
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised Unimed, a third-party billing service provider used by multiple German university hospitals, in mid-April and exfiltrated patient billing records.
incidents.impact: Roughly 97,000+ patients affected across the hospitals (about 30,000 in Cologne, 54,000 in Freiburg, 11,000 in Heidelberg, 1,600 in Ulm). Stolen data includes names, addresses, treating physicians, and in thousands of cases diagnosis or billing information; bank data was exposed in a small number of cases.

incidents.vector: Hackers gained access to systems holding patient records and biometric enrollment data; the initial intrusion vector has not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: At least 1.8 million people affected. Stolen records include medical data and biometric identifiers such as fingerprints and palm prints, which cannot be reissued and create permanent identity risk for victims.

incidents.vector: TeamPCP poisoned a Visual Studio Code extension that was installed on a GitHub employee's device, granting access to thousands of internal GitHub source code repositories.
incidents.impact: Approximately 3,800 internal source-code repositories accessed and offered for sale at $50,000 with a leak threat. GitHub says no customer data was affected and that critical credentials were rotated the same day the breach was detected.

incidents.victim: TanStack, Mistral, UiPath, OpenAI and ~400 open-source packages
incidents.vector: Self-replicating Shai-Hulud worm propagated through compromised npm/PyPI packages including the TanStack React framework, harvesting developer credentials, API keys, cloud tokens and crypto wallets from infected developer machines.
incidents.impact: Almost 400 packages compromised, including libraries at Mistral and UiPath. OpenAI confirmed two employee devices were impacted and is rotating code-signing certificates. The worm's source code was subsequently leaked on a hacking forum with a $10,000 bounty offered for further attacks, raising risk of follow-on supply chain campaigns.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited the Verus-Ethereum cross-chain bridge.
incidents.impact: $11.58 million in crypto assets stolen.

incidents.victim: Pierre & Vacances, Belambra, Gîtes de France
incidents.vector: Three French holiday-booking platforms were breached by the same individual hacker; the specific intrusion vector has not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: Customer data from all three platforms was stolen and offered for sale online.

incidents.victim: U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
incidents.vector: A contractor from Nightwing maintained a public 'Private-CISA' GitHub repository that exposed AWS GovCloud admin keys, plaintext credentials and an RSA private key for a CISA GitHub app; the contractor had explicitly disabled GitHub's built-in secret-scanning protections.
incidents.impact: Dozens of CISA internal system credentials and source-code build infrastructure exposed publicly since at least November 2025. A week after notification CISA was still rotating leaked credentials. Researchers warn cybercriminal groups and foreign adversaries that monitor GitHub's public commit firehose may have collected the secrets; Congress has demanded answers and a classified briefing.

incidents.victim: Screening Serpens campaign targets (U.S., Israel, UAE, additional Middle Eastern entities)
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing emails impersonating global airlines and video-conferencing brands delivered ZIP archives with fake job descriptions; execution of the bundled installer triggered DLL sideloading and AppDomainManager hijacking to deploy six new RAT variants (MiniUpdate and MiniJunk V2).
incidents.impact: Coordinated espionage campaign timed with the regional Middle East conflict ran from mid-February through April. Targets included aerospace, defense and technology professionals in the U.S., Israel, UAE and other Middle Eastern entities. The campaign demonstrates significant evolution in the group's technical capability and operational resilience.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of a zero-day cross-site scripting flaw (CVE-2026-42897) in Exchange Outlook Web Access; a crafted email opened in OWA executes arbitrary JavaScript in the user's browser session.
incidents.impact: Mailbox compromise: attackers can read mail, steal session tokens, alter mailbox settings and plant forwarding rules that survive password resets, providing initial access for business email compromise and ransomware operations. Microsoft has issued mitigations via the Emergency Mitigation Service but no full patch is yet available; CISA added the flaw to its KEV catalog.

incidents.victim: BlackFile/UNC6671 victims across North America, Australia and the UK
incidents.vector: Voice phishing of employees impersonating IT help desks under a passkey/MFA enrollment pretext; live adversary-in-the-middle credential harvesting against Microsoft 365 and Okta SSO; automated Python and PowerShell scripts then exfiltrated SharePoint, OneDrive, Salesforce and Zendesk data using stolen session cookies.
incidents.impact: Dozens of organizations targeted in 2026. In one case attackers exfiltrated more than a million files from a single victim. Extortion demands have ranged into the millions, escalating to spam floods against executives, threatening voicemails and even swatting when victims refuse to engage.

incidents.victim: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller and Manager customers (including U.S. federal agencies)
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of CVE-2026-20182, a pre-authentication authentication-bypass flaw (CVSS 10) in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller and Manager that lets attackers impersonate a trusted router and obtain administrative privileges. Talos attributes the activity to UAT-8616, the same nation-state cluster behind earlier Cisco edge zero-day campaigns.
incidents.impact: Attackers added SSH keys, modified NETCONF configurations and escalated to root on compromised SD-WAN controllers, enabling traffic interception and lateral movement across enterprise overlays. CISA ordered all federal civilian agencies to patch by May 17; an additional 10+ threat clusters are also chaining three previously-patched SD-WAN flaws to deploy webshells.

incidents.vector: A rogue version of Checkmarx's official Jenkins Application Security Testing plugin was published on the Jenkins Marketplace containing an infostealer.
incidents.impact: Checkmarx warned customers that the compromised plugin could exfiltrate developer credentials and CI/CD secrets from organizations that installed it before the rogue version was pulled.

incidents.vector: A malicious repository impersonating OpenAI's open-weight 'Privacy Filter' model climbed to the top of the Hugging Face trending list and shipped a Rust-based information stealer to Windows users.
incidents.impact: 244,000 downloads of the trojanized model before it was removed; potential theft of developer credentials, tokens and other secrets on infected machines.

incidents.vector: The Nitrogen ransomware group breached Foxconn's North American manufacturing network and deployed ransomware that disrupted plant operations and stole production data.
incidents.impact: Wi-Fi outages and computer disruption at Wisconsin and other North American facilities forced employees to work on paper. Nitrogen claims to have stolen 8 TB / 11 million files including confidential project data tied to Apple, Intel, Google, Dell and Nvidia. Foxconn says affected factories are resuming normal production.

incidents.victim: City of Arcadia, California / U.S. local political institutions
incidents.vector: Arcadia Mayor Eileen Wang received and executed directives from PRC government officials over WeChat, posting pro-Beijing propaganda articles drafted by Chinese officials on a Chinese-American 'news' website she co-operated, and coordinating with a high-level PRC intelligence figure.
incidents.impact: A sitting U.S. mayor was federally charged with acting as an illegal foreign agent and has agreed to plead guilty (up to 10 years in prison). The case underscores continued PRC efforts to influence U.S. local political institutions and diaspora media.

incidents.vector: On May 4 attackers breached West Pharmaceutical's network, exfiltrated data and encrypted critical systems; the company filed an 8-K with the SEC on May 11.
incidents.impact: Globally disrupted shipping, receiving and manufacturing for one of the largest providers of injectable drug-delivery components (more than 10,000 employees, $3 billion+ in 2025 sales). Core enterprise systems have been restored at some sites but full restoration timeline is not finalized; Unit 42 leads the investigation.

incidents.vector: ShinyHunters breached Instructure's Canvas platform and, after a stalled extortion negotiation, defaced the Canvas login page with a ransom demand directed at affected schools.
incidents.impact: Canvas was taken offline during final-exam season, disrupting classes at nearly 9,000 schools and universities. ShinyHunters claims to hold data on roughly 275 million students and faculty, including names, email addresses, student IDs and messages; some universities are reportedly negotiating ransom payments directly.

incidents.vector: ShinyHunters breached 7-Eleven in April and listed the company on its dark-web leak site; the specific intrusion vector has not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: 7-Eleven has formally notified state authorities (Maine OAG filing) of a data breach. Scope and number of records affected have not been publicly quantified.

incidents.victim: RXNT (and downstream patients including members of U.S. Congress)
incidents.vector: Attackers breached RXNT, a drug-prescription software platform, in March; the intrusion vector has not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: Patient data stolen, including data on members of the U.S. Congress that use RXNT for prescriptions. RXNT notified authorities on the final day allowed under U.S. health privacy law.
